# Installation and quick start {#installation}

This chapter gives a complete, reproducible path from installation to the first
rendered figures. The rest of the manual assumes this setup.

## Installation options

There are three supported installation modes:

1. Install the **umbrella package** only (`glyphome`) for shared theme helpers
   and the render-all driver.
2. Install the umbrella plus all ten module packages.
3. Install only one module package, such as `densweave` or `survivora`.

### System requirements

`glyphome` is intentionally lightweight, but several graphics dependencies
compile native code. On Linux, install these once:

```{bash eval=FALSE}
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential libxml2-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev \
  libssl-dev libfontconfig1-dev libharfbuzz-dev libfribidi-dev \
  libfreetype6-dev libpng-dev libtiff5-dev libjpeg-dev
```

On macOS, install Xcode Command Line Tools:

```{bash eval=FALSE}
xcode-select --install
```

On Windows, install the matching Rtools release from CRAN.

### Install from GitHub

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("isadeghi87/glyphome")
```

Then install all ten modules:

```{r eval=FALSE}
modules <- c(
  "uncertainr", "provtrace", "scalefusion", "counterpath", "intercapsule",
  "densweave", "clinladder", "survivora", "cohortprism", "riskweave"
)

for (m in modules) {
  remotes::install_github("isadeghi87/glyphome", subdir = file.path("packages", m))
}
```

### Install only one module

```{r eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github("isadeghi87/glyphome", subdir = "packages/densweave")
library(densweave)
densweave_plot_atlas()
```

This is recommended when you only need one grammar family and want to keep the
runtime environment minimal.

## Quick start from a clone

Clone the repository and render all figures:

```{bash eval=FALSE}
git clone https://github.com/isadeghi87/glyphome.git
cd glyphome
Rscript scripts/generate_all_figures.R
```

The script writes the curated PNG set to `figures/`. To render only a subset:

```{bash eval=FALSE}
Rscript scripts/generate_all_figures.R --module densweave survivora
```

## Quick start inside R

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(glyphome)

glyphome_load_all()            # source every module into the session
glyphome_render_all("figures") # render the curated figure set
```

A single module can be sourced directly during development:

```{r eval=FALSE}
source("R/glyphome-common.R")
source("packages/densweave/R/densweave.R")

densweave_plot_atlas()
```

## Common workflow

The recommended workflow is:

1. Generate or load a tidy analysis table.
2. Convert it to a module-specific data structure if needed.
3. Call the module plot constructor.
4. Apply shared theme or adjust module parameters.
5. Save with role-aware sizing.
6. Assemble final composites only after panel-level QC.

```{r eval=FALSE}
source("R/glyphome-common.R")
source("packages/riskweave/R/riskweave.R")

p <- riskweave_plot_frontier()
glyphome_save(p, "figures/risk_frontier.png", role = "primary")
```

## Building this tutorial

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("bookdown")
bookdown::render_book("book/")
browseURL("book/_book/index.html")
```

The rendered HTML is a local artifact and is not required for using the package.

## Troubleshooting

### `there is no package called 'ggnewscale'`

Install CRAN dependencies explicitly:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("ggplot2", "patchwork", "dplyr", "tidyr", "scales",
                   "MASS", "ggraph", "igraph", "ggnewscale", "bookdown"))
```

### GitHub installation fails over SSH

Use HTTPS instead:

```{bash eval=FALSE}
git clone https://github.com/isadeghi87/glyphome.git
```

### Figures render but text is too small

Use a larger base theme or role size:

```{r eval=FALSE}
p + glyphome_theme(base_size = 13)
glyphome_save(p, "large_panel.png", role = "hero")
```
